title: Unit economics: fully loaded cost per customer, labelled payback, revenue churn and expansion, no uncapped LTV
decision_task: Whether a play pays back, and which payback number and benchmark to show the owner. / Which costs count in cost per customer. / Which churn drives value and payback, and whether expansion counts. / How to express customer value.
applies_when: Any play with revenue per customer, gross margin, churn and a CAC.
Every play cost and every observed channel CAC.
Recurring businesses with customers of different sizes, or with upsell, usage or seat pricing.
exclusions: Churn is unknown. ClimbOS already returns null (economics.ts:206); keep that behaviour.
One-off purchase businesses: use repeat rate instead.
required_inputs: Revenue per customer per month (cohorts.ts revenueMinor)
evidence_requirements: Contribution or gross margin with its cost boundary
Monthly churn with its type (customer or revenue)
Owner and staff hours with their value
Tools, freelancers, creative, data and ClimbOS credits attributable to the play
Monthly MRR lost from churn and downgrades
missing_data_behavior: Churn unknown: value and payback stay null (current behaviour).
Non-media costs unknown: ask; label CAC as excluding them.
Expansion unknown: assume none and say so.
alternatives_when_constrained: Missing churn: show only the no-churn payback, labelled as an upper bound on speed, with no verdict.
No cohorts: use the owner's churn, tagged as an assumption.
Small sample: give a range across churn of 0.5×–2× (economics.ts:405 already does this).
Missing hours: use the default $50 per hour (economics.ts:83-88), flagged as assumed.
No tool costs known: show 0 and mark it 'not included'.
Missing revenue churn: fall back to customer churn, labelled 'customer churn used as proxy'.
Missing churn: show no value at all (current behaviour).

decision_branches.if: Small customers churn more than large
decision_branches.then: Revenue churn below customer churn: use revenue churn for value.
Replace with 12-month value; benchmarks carry era and basis.

implementation_steps: Compute the GM-adjusted no-churn payback (DS-FX3) and the churn-weighted payback (DS-FX4).
Use the churn-weighted figure for the verdict.
Show both, labelled 'per surviving customer' and 'expected, with churn'.
When citing external benchmarks, attach their era and basis (no churn, GM ≥ 80%, venture-backed).
Add an 'other monthly costs' input per play (tools, freelance, creative, data).
Pass it to cacFull instead of 0 (economics.ts:203).
Show media-only CAC next to it (calc.ts:28-32).
Put retention and account-management costs (Skok's CORE) in gross margin, not in CAC.
Ask or measure customer churn and revenue churn separately.
Use net revenue churn for value and payback, capped at 12 months (DS-EX4).
Use customer churn for customer-count goals (goal.ts:71).
Keep 12-month churn-weighted contribution as the allowable CAC.
If a longer view is wanted, show 24-month value discounted at a stated rate and labelled as a forecast.
guardrails: Never compare the churn-weighted payback with Skok's '<12' or '5–7 months' without a label.
Never present LTV:CAC 3× as a pass/fail test.
Do not apply Skok's early-stage practice of counting only part of senior salaries to owner time; for an owner-operator those hours do not scale away (DS-02-F10).
Never let negative net churn produce unbounded value; keep the 12-month cap.
Expansion must be observed, or tagged as an assumption.
Never show LTV = ARPA × GM / churn as a headline.
observation_window: 12 months, the ClimbOS horizon (economics.ts:89-90). / The play horizon (economics.ts:193). / Monthly, read over at least 3 complete months. / 12 months.
stop_conditions: Re-run when the owner confirms churn or margin.
Re-run when observed cohort churn differs from the input by 50% or more.
Review when a cost category is added or removed.
Review if expansion assumed above 0 is not observed within 90 days.
review_triggers: Owner corrects an input this playbook relies on
A metric or guardrail crosses its bound
The underlying source or platform rule changes

interpretation: Interpretation: Skok's payback is per surviving customer. ClimbOS's is an expected value over a decaying cohort, which is stricter and better suited to owner-funded businesses.
Interpretation: valuing owner time at an hourly rate is a ClimbOS extension. It is consistent with Skok's rule of no exclusions, though Skok never mentions founder time.
Interpretation: ClimbOS's single churn field mixes the customer and revenue concepts.
Interpretation: Skok's own 2016 revision supports ClimbOS's capped approach.
proposed_climbos_rule: Proposed rule: the locked numbers show 'payback X months with churn (Y months per surviving customer)'. Benchmarks always carry era and basis.
Proposed rule: cacFull receives the play's non-media costs. The margin question (economics.ts:381) asks for cost 'to deliver and keep' a customer.
Proposed rule: add monthlyRevenueChurn and monthlyExpansion as optional inputs. The value formula uses (1 + g)(1 − c_rev), with g and c_rev both observed or tagged as assumed.
Proposed rule: keep as is, and add a lint that rejects any plan text quoting a lifetime value or a 3× rule.
disagreements: Skok later accepted 18–24 month paybacks for well-capitalised companies. ClimbOS's 12-month horizon follows Skok's own reasoning that startups without cheap capital cannot wait, so for small businesses 12 is defensible.
Skok's expansion LTV uses linear dollar growth; the proposal uses compound growth over 12 months. Both are labelled simplifications.
Skok still treats LTV as useful for comparing segments. ClimbOS can compare segments on 12-month value instead.
